ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Three-level cascade with layer skipping above prompt lookup
PROPOSAL: Build a vertical cascade on Vicuna-13B-v1.3 in which prompt lookup decoding (n-gram size 3) sits at the bottom, a layer-skipping drafter derived from the target itself (about 40% of blocks skipped, chosen by a short Bayesian search on 50 calibration prompts) sits in the middle, and the full target verifies. Measure walltime speedup, mean accepted tokens per target pass and the acceptance rate of each level on MT-Bench, CNN/DailyMail and GSM8K, using 80 prompts per dataset, batch size 1 and greedy decoding. Choose the draft length of each level from a small grid on held-out prompts, then freeze it before testing.
CONTROLS: Plain autoregressive decoding; prompt lookup alone; the layer-skipping drafter alone; the two-level cascade without lookup; a token-identity check against greedy decoding on all test generations.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The cascade should beat lookup alone by roughly 1.2x on MT-Bench and summarization, but may fail to improve on GSM8K, where the acceptance rate of the skipped-layer drafter may be too low for its latency. The gain would also vanish if that drafter takes more than half a target pass.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cascade of lookup, layer skipping and verifier on two target models
PROPOSAL: Evaluate a cascade of prompt lookup, layer skipping and the verifying target on Llama-2-13B-chat and Vicuna-33B, covering the 6 Spec-Bench categories with 160 prompts each. Re-run the layer-skip search for each model and category pair with 200 calibration prompts and 5 seeds, and select the draft length of each level from a grid re-optimised on each combination. Record speedup, mean accepted length and per-level acceptance at batch size 1 with greedy decoding, together with a latency profile of each drafter at 3 prompt lengths.
CONTROLS: Autoregressive decoding and prompt lookup alone on each model; the layer-skipping drafter alone; a cascade using the default skip pattern released with SWIFT; token-identity checks against greedy output on all generations.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Speedups over prompt lookup of 10 to 25 percent are expected on conversation and summarization, with the smallest gains on mathematical reasoning. The best skip pattern may differ little between categories, in which case the per-category search brings nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Acceptance-driven draft length for a lookup and early-exit cascade
PROPOSAL: Replace the fixed draft lengths of a two-level cascade (prompt lookup below, early-exit drafting from layer 20 in the target above) with a controller that tracks an exponential moving average of the per-token acceptance rate and sets the next draft length by maximising the analytic expected speedup, using measured latency ratios. Test on Llama-2-7B-chat with MT-Bench, XSum and Natural Questions, 60 prompts each, greedy decoding, batch size 1. Calibrate the latency ratios once from 20 timing runs, then freeze them before testing.
CONTROLS: Best fixed draft length per level found on a held-out split; the same controller with smoothing set to 0 (acceptance of the last step only); an oracle schedule from offline per-step acceptance traces; a lossless check against greedy decoding.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Adaptive lengths should give 5 to 10 percent over the best fixed schedule on mixed prompts. The gain may disappear on summarization, where acceptance is stable, and controller overhead could cancel it on short outputs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Draft length controllers for a lookup and early-exit cascade
PROPOSAL: Compare controllers that set draft length in a two-level cascade of prompt lookup and early-exit drafting, using Llama-2-7B-chat and Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct on MT-Bench, XSum, Natural Questions, HumanEval, GSM8K and WMT14 De-En with 100 prompts each. Implement a moving-average controller, a UCB bandit, a Thompson sampler and a small recurrent predictor trained on logged traces from a separate collection run, tuning the smoothing or exploration setting of each over a grid, with 3 seeds, at two batch sizes. Record speedup, accepted length and controller overhead at each step.
CONTROLS: Best fixed length per level for each model and dataset; an oracle built from offline traces; random lengths drawn uniformly between the smallest and largest allowed; a lossless check against greedy decoding.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Adaptive controllers should beat the best fixed schedule by about 5 percent on mixed prompts, with the bandits ahead on short outputs. At the higher batch size the benefit may vanish because verification dominates the step.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bandit selection among training-free drafters inside one generation
PROPOSAL: Treat each self-speculative drafter (layer skipping, early exit, Jacobi-style parallel decoding) and prompt lookup as arms of a contextual bandit that is queried at each verification round. The reward is accepted tokens per unit of measured latency. Run Thompson sampling with a Beta posterior per arm, reset at each prompt and warm-started from an acceptance table measured on 100 training prompts. Use Llama-2-13B-chat on MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K and CNN/DailyMail with 100 test prompts each, greedy decoding, batch size 1, and report speedup with 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Each drafter used alone; prompt lookup alone; the best single static cascade found on training prompts; an oracle that picks the best arm per round from logged acceptances; token-identity check against greedy decoding.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The bandit should land within 5 percent of the oracle on code and summarization, where one arm dominates for long stretches, and give a smaller gain on mathematics. Posterior resets at each prompt may cost more than they save on outputs shorter than 100 tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Policy comparison for switching between self-derived drafters
PROPOSAL: Compare switching policies among layer skipping, early exit, Jacobi decoding, Lookahead decoding and prompt lookup at each verification round, on Llama-2-13B-chat and Qwen-14B-chat. Policies are Thompson sampling, UCB, epsilon-greedy over a ladder of epsilons, a softmax rule over a ladder of temperatures and a gradient-boosted predictor trained on logged acceptances, each tuned on its own validation split. Use MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, CNN/DailyMail, WMT14 De-En and NQ with 150 prompts each, greedy decoding, batch sizes 1 and 8, 5 seeds, and log speedup at each round.
CONTROLS: Each drafter alone; prompt lookup alone; the best static cascade per model; an oracle from logged acceptances; a uniformly random policy; token-identity check against greedy decoding.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Learned policies should land within 5 to 8 percent of the oracle on code and summarization, with little to gain on mathematics. The gradient-boosted predictor may lose to simple bandits once overhead per round is included.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Horizontal cascade: slow accurate start, fast tail
PROPOSAL: Draft the first two tokens of each round with the early-exit drafter taken at layer 24 of Vicuna-13B-v1.3, then continue the draft with prompt lookup until its n-gram match fails, and verify with the full model. Vary the number of tokens drafted by the early-exit stage from 1 to 3, and the lookup n-gram size from 2 to 4. Evaluate on MT-Bench, CNN/DailyMail, GSM8K and HumanEval with 80 prompts each, greedy decoding, batch size 1. Report accepted tokens by position in the draft and walltime speedup.
CONTROLS: Early-exit drafting alone; prompt lookup alone; a vertical cascade with the same two drafters; a horizontal cascade where the order of the drafters is reversed; a lossless check against greedy output.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Accuracy of the first draft positions should dominate, giving about 1.15x over prompt lookup on conversation and code. The horizontal form may match the vertical one on repetitive summaries, where lookup alone already accepts long runs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Position-aware schedules built from layer skipping, early exit and lookup
PROPOSAL: Study horizontal and vertical schedules built from layer skipping, early exit, Lookahead and prompt lookup on Llama-2-7B-chat and Qwen-14B-chat. Each schedule hands the first few positions to a slower drafter and the rest to faster ones, with lookup n-gram sizes from 2 to 5 and a fresh calibration split for each combination and a reversed-order variant of each schedule. Evaluate on MT-Bench, CNN/DailyMail, HumanEval, GSM8K, WMT14 De-En and NQ with 120 prompts each, greedy decoding, batch size 1, 5 seeds. Report accepted tokens by position, speedup and the best schedule per dataset.
CONTROLS: Each drafter alone; a single vertical cascade per model; a schedule with the drafter order reversed; a schedule with random assignment of positions to drafters; lossless check against greedy output.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Position-aware schedules should gain 10 to 20 percent over prompt lookup on conversation and code, and little on repetitive summaries. Differences between the schedule shapes may fall within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hardware dependence of cascade speedups for training-free drafters
PROPOSAL: Measure how the best cascade of layer skipping and prompt lookup changes with the accelerator. Time the draft and verify steps of Llama-2-13B-chat on an Ampere server card, a Hopper card and an Ada workstation card at batch size 1, and fit the latency ratio of each drafter to the target. Feed the ratios and acceptance rates measured on 150 MT-Bench and 150 CNN/DailyMail prompts into the analytic walltime model to predict the best draft lengths per device. Then run the predicted and the transferred configuration on each device with 3 seeds, greedy decoding, and compare the speedups.
CONTROLS: A cascade tuned on one device and moved unchanged to the others; prompt lookup alone on each device; plain decoding; the analytic prediction compared with measured speedups; a lossless check against greedy output.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Latency ratios should differ by 10 to 30 percent between devices, which shifts the best draft length by one or two tokens. The transferred configuration should lose under 5 percent, so device-specific tuning may turn out to be of thin value.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Device-specific tuning of cascades with layer skipping, Jacobi decoding and lookup
PROPOSAL: Time the draft and verify steps of Llama-2-7B-chat and Vicuna-33B on five accelerator types, from consumer to datacenter cards, at three batch sizes, and fit the latency ratio of layer skipping, early exit, Jacobi decoding, Lookahead and prompt lookup to the target. Use 300 prompts from MT-Bench, CNN/DailyMail, HumanEval, GSM8K, WMT14 De-En and NQ to measure acceptance, then run a full grid of draft lengths per level on each device with 4 seeds. Compare tuned and transferred settings, and report the idle time of each drafter between verification rounds.
CONTROLS: A configuration tuned on one device and moved unchanged to the others; prompt lookup alone on each device; plain decoding; analytic predictions against measured speedups; lossless check against greedy output.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Latency ratios should vary by 10 to 30 percent between devices, moving the best draft length by one or two tokens. Transferred settings should lose under 5 percent, so the tuning may bring little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Acceptance rate traces within single sequences
PROPOSAL: Record, for each verification round, the accepted length of layer skipping, early exit and prompt lookup on Llama-2-7B-chat while it generates answers to 60 prompts from MT-Bench, GSM8K and HumanEval (20 each). Segment each output into 32-token windows and fit a mixed-effects model with fixed effects for drafter and window position and a random effect for prompt. Report how much variance in acceptance lies within sequences compared with between sequences, and what a per-window oracle choice of drafter would gain over the best fixed choice, Bonferroni-corrected.
CONTROLS: Variance decomposition from a null model with prompt effect only; shuffled-window baseline that destroys positional structure; best fixed drafter per dataset; bootstrap intervals over prompts; lossless check against greedy output.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: Within-sequence variance should account for more than a third of the total for prompt lookup, which depends on local repetition, and less for layer skipping. The per-window oracle should gain 10 to 15 percent, and the positional effect may be weak on mathematics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Acceptance rate traces for five drafters on six task families
PROPOSAL: Record the accepted length of layer skipping, early exit, Jacobi decoding, Lookahead and prompt lookup at each verification round for Llama-2-13B and Qwen-14B on 600 prompts from MT-Bench, GSM8K, HumanEval, XSum, WMT14 and NQ. Segment outputs into windows of a few different lengths and fit a mixed-effects model with fixed effects for drafter, window position and window length and random effects for prompt, refitting for 4 seeds of the sampling split. Report within-sequence and between-sequence variance and a per-window oracle gain, together with the share of rounds in which each drafter would have been the fastest.
CONTROLS: Variance decomposition from a null model with prompt effect only; shuffled-window baseline; best fixed drafter per dataset; bootstrap intervals over prompts; lossless check against greedy output.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: More than a third of the acceptance variance of prompt lookup should lie within sequences, and less for layer skipping. A per-window oracle should gain 10 to 15 percent, though window length may matter little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Number of cascade rounds and walltime: analytic model against measurement
PROPOSAL: Fit the analytic walltime model of cascades, with each level described by expected acceptance rate and relative latency, to measured speedups of Llama-2-13B-chat when the cascade has 1, 2 or 3 nested rounds of layer skipping and early exit above prompt lookup. Measure acceptance and latency on 200 prompts from MT-Bench, CNN/DailyMail, GSM8K and HumanEval, predict the best number of rounds and draft lengths on 100 held-out prompts, then run the predicted and neighbouring settings with 3 seeds. Report prediction error in speedup.
CONTROLS: Single-level speculative decoding with prompt lookup; the two-level cascade; the model with acceptance rates held constant rather than measured per position; a lossless check against greedy decoding.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The model should predict speedup within 8 percent and show that a third round helps only when acceptance exceeds 0.8. Gains over two levels may be under 3 percent, which is within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Depth of cascade and walltime for models of three families
PROPOSAL: Fit the analytic walltime model of cascades to measured speedups of Llama-2-7B-chat, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct and Qwen-14B-chat, when the cascade nests up to 5 rounds built from layer skipping, early exit, Jacobi decoding, Lookahead and prompt lookup. Measure acceptance and latency on 600 prompts from MT-Bench, CNN/DailyMail, HumanEval, GSM8K, WMT14 De-En and NQ, predict the best depth and draft lengths on 300 held-out prompts, then run neighbouring settings with 4 seeds and repeat the fit for each model and dataset.
CONTROLS: Single-level speculative decoding with prompt lookup; the two-level cascade; the model with acceptance rates held constant; a lossless check against greedy decoding.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The model should predict speedup within 8 percent and show that deeper cascades help only when acceptance exceeds 0.8. Gains beyond two levels may be under 3 percent, within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Early exit against layer skipping as the middle level
PROPOSAL: Decide which training-free technique should supply the middle level of a cascade above prompt lookup. On Llama-2-13B-chat, build one cascade with early-exit drafting at layer 24, one with layer skipping of 40% of blocks, and one with Lookahead decoding using window 7 and n-gram size 5. Compare walltime speedup, accepted length and drafter latency relative to the target on MT-Bench, CNN/DailyMail, GSM8K, HumanEval and NQ with 80 prompts each, batch size 1, greedy decoding, using 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup alone; each middle-level technique used without lookup beneath it; the three cascades with the middle level removed; token-identity check against greedy output.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Early exit should win on conversation by roughly 10 percent through lower latency, and layer skipping should win on code through higher acceptance. Lookahead may lose to lookup alone, as reported for the original methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Choice of middle level among four techniques with tuned settings
PROPOSAL: Decide which training-free technique should supply the middle level of a cascade above prompt lookup. Build cascades with early-exit drafting, layer skipping, Lookahead decoding and Jacobi decoding on Llama-2-7B-chat and Vicuna-33B, tuning the exit layer, skipped fraction, window and n-gram size of each over a grid on a dedicated split. Compare speedup, accepted length and drafter latency on MT-Bench, CNN/DailyMail, HumanEval, GSM8K, WMT14 De-En and NQ with 120 prompts each at batch size 1 and greedy decoding, with 4 seeds.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup alone; each technique used without lookup beneath it; the cascades with the middle level removed; token-identity check against greedy output.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Early exit should win on conversation by roughly 10 percent through lower latency, layer skipping on code through higher acceptance. Lookahead may lose to lookup alone, as reported for the original methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lossless behaviour of cascades under sampling
PROPOSAL: Check that a cascade of layer skipping and prompt lookup preserves the target distribution when decoding with temperature 0.7 and nucleus sampling at 0.9. Use Llama-2-7B-chat and a set of 40 prompts. For each prompt, draw 1000 completions of 16 tokens from plain decoding and from the cascade, and compare empirical distributions over the first 3 token positions with a chi-square test and total variation distance. Then measure speedup under sampling on MT-Bench and CNN/DailyMail with 80 prompts each.
CONTROLS: Standard speculative decoding with one drafter as a sanity case; an incorrect acceptance rule with a corrupted ratio as a positive control for the test; two independent plain decoding samples compared with each other for the null distribution.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: No distributional difference should be found beyond the null spread, and speedup under sampling should be 10 to 20 percent below the greedy case because acceptance falls. The test may lack power at the third position.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distribution tests of cascades under temperature and nucleus sampling
PROPOSAL: Check that cascades built from layer skipping, early exit, Jacobi decoding and prompt lookup preserve the target distribution when sampling at a ladder of temperatures with nucleus values 0.8 and 0.95, on Llama-2-13B-chat and Qwen-14B-chat. For 120 prompts, draw 2000 completions of 32 tokens from plain decoding and from each cascade, and compare distributions over the first 6 token positions with chi-square tests and total variation distance. Then measure speedup under each sampling setting on MT-Bench, GSM8K, HumanEval and CNN/DailyMail with 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Standard speculative decoding with one drafter as a sanity case; a wrong acceptance rule with a corrupted ratio as a positive control; two independent plain decoding samples compared with each other for the null distribution.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: No distributional difference should appear beyond the null spread, and speedup under sampling should be 10 to 20 percent below the greedy case. Tests at the later positions may have low power.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt-feature router for cascade configuration
PROPOSAL: Train a gradient-boosted router that picks one of four cascade configurations (prompt lookup alone, lookup plus early exit, lookup plus layer skipping, lookup plus both) from features available before decoding: prompt length, fraction of prompt n-grams that recur, task tag, and the target's first-token entropy. Collect acceptance logs of Llama-2-13B-chat on 1200 prompts from benchmark datasets, label the fastest configuration per prompt, and test the router on 300 held-out prompts with 5-fold cross-validation.
CONTROLS: Each fixed configuration; a router using task tag only; a random router; an oracle choosing the fastest configuration per prompt; lossless check against greedy decoding.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: The router should recover 70 percent of the oracle gain over the best fixed configuration, with prompt repetition as the most informative feature. It may add little on tasks where one configuration wins for nearly all prompts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned router over twelve cascade configurations and prompt features
PROPOSAL: Train gradient-boosted and small neural routers that choose among twelve cascade configurations built from prompt lookup, early exit, layer skipping and Lookahead decoding, using prompt length, recurring n-gram fraction, task tag, first-token entropy, embedding statistics and the acceptance seen in the first rounds. Collect logs of Llama-2-7B-chat and Qwen-14B-chat on 3000 prompts from six benchmark datasets, label the fastest configuration for each prompt, and test on 600 held-out prompts with cross-validation folds stratified by dataset and 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Each fixed configuration; a router using task tag only; a random router; an oracle choosing the fastest configuration per prompt; lossless check against greedy decoding.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Routers should recover about 70 percent of the oracle gain over the best fixed configuration, with recurring n-gram fraction the most informative feature. Little gain is expected where one configuration wins for nearly all prompts.
